clue.text: Directive popular with union

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a junction is a joining or union of things

explanation.surface: An order issued with the backing of a well-liked trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order directing someone to do or refrain from doing something is a kind of directive.

clue.text: Mountain goat from central Tibet? Spot marked

indicators.note: central says to take the inner letters of Tibet, losing its ends

parts.note: X marks the spot, as on a treasure map

explanation.surface: An animal found in the heart of Tibet at a marked location.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat with long curved horns living in high mountains.

clue.text: Containers and nicer jars smashed

indicators.note: smashed says the letters of these words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Receptacles and some pleasant pots get broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerricans are flat-sided metal containers for fuel or water.

clue.text: Material vital to many Londoners

indicators.note: vital to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fabric that plenty of people in the capital can't do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a kind of textile material.

clue.text: Given medical attention and not asked to pay

definitions.meaning: seen to by a doctor or nurse
bought a meal or drink by someone else

explanation.surface: A patient was cared for and had no bill to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both being nursed by a doctor and being bought something as a gift.

clue.text: Work with uranium, fast becoming rich

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Handling radioactive metal quickly makes someone wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun: Lent is a time of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly wealthy or luxurious, a synonym of rich.

clue.text: Assumed name I omitted, unfortunately

indicators.note: omitted says the letter I is left out of the false name

parts.note: an alias is a name someone assumes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having left their pen name off something.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection expressing regret, used exactly where one would say sadly or unfortunately.

clue.text: Sound of composer's records

indicators.note: sound of says the answer is pronounced like the clue's word for the composer's

parts.note: Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist

explanation.surface: The tone of a musician's albums.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists are written records of items, and to list is to record them.

clue.text: Cover international actor's trial

parts.note: to screen is to shield or cover
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Someone covering for a global film star at an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international game, especially in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition to judge an actor's suitability for a role.

clue.text: Exhausted? Everyone, on the whole

parts.note: all in means tired out
all means every person

explanation.surface: Asking whether people are tired, and concluding everybody is, by and large.
explanation.definitionFit: All in all means taking everything into account, generally, or on the whole.

clue.text: Learning about name written backwards in register

indicators.note: written backwards says the assembled letters are read from right to left
about says the word for learning goes round the abbreviation for name

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: A student learns to write their name in reverse when signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside LORE to make LORNE, and 'written backwards' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to put one's name down on a list, which is the verb sense of register.

clue.text: What could make one lie square?

definitions.text: What could make one lie square?

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the following two words can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: Something that might set an untruth straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a levelling goal: it makes one side lie square with the other, and those two words rearranged also give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The goal or point that brings the scores level is what makes a team stand level with its rivals.

clue.text: Character sketch: get vet in, comically

indicators.note: comically says the letters of the following words are jumbled in a funny way

explanation.surface: A writer describes a farmer calling out the animal doctor for laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a brief descriptive piece of writing, often portraying a person.

clue.text: Publish paper with no leader

indicators.note: with no leader says the first letter of the word for paper is dropped

parts.note: tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper goes to press without its editorial column or its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like a newspaper editorial or chief, but it just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or statement is to bring it out publicly, a synonym of publish.

clue.text: Florid fellow guarding lad in apartment

indicators.note: in says the guarding pair sits inside the word for apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: guarding says the word for fellow surrounds the word for lad

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: An ornate man protects a youngster in his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florid fellow' tempts a solver to look for a flashy man; 'fellow' is only the wrapper for the lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant means showy and elaborate, close in sense to florid in style.

clue.text: King Edward, well-informed

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
Ned is a familiar form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A monarch called Edward who is said to be knowledgeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person has acquired much knowledge through study, so is well-informed.

clue.text: Ship from North America, with nothing on board, heading for Holy Island

indicators.note: on board says the letter for nothing sits inside the abbreviation, like a passenger

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A vessel leaves America empty and sails for a sacred island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small island in the English Channel. 'Holy Island' suggests Lindisfarne, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's Ark is the vessel built by Noah in Genesis to survive the Flood.

clue.text: Passage from 'North and South' in characteristic setting

indicators.note: setting says the word for characteristic forms a mount round the compass letters, like a jewel's setting

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
N is the compass abbreviation for north
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: An extract taken from the novel North and South in its typical setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North and South' looks like the Gaskell novel title; it supplies N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across, a passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Edited memoirs involving the Spanish steward

indicators.note: involving says the rearranged letters surround the Spanish word
edited says the word memoirs is reworked into a new order

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A revised autobiography includes a Spanish waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steward' here is the wine steward of a restaurant, not a ship's or estate's steward.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine steward in a restaurant.

clue.text: Pole on motorway makes error

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the word for pole after the motorway letters

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
a stake is a pole driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A post put up on a motorway turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is a slip or blunder, the same as an error.

clue.text: Note hidden in cake is not in code

indicators.note: hidden in says the letter for note is concealed inside the pastry

parts.note: an eclair is a cream-filled pastry cake
N is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote

explanation.surface: A secret message has been baked inside a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair is a French phrase for a message sent in plain language rather than cipher.

clue.text: I'm 6, taken back to small island

indicators.note: taken back says the first two pieces are read in reverse order of letters

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped
the answer to 6 Across, the regretful interjection, is used here

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for themselves heads back to a tiny isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Across is ALAS; IMALAS reversed gives SALAMI, then S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamis is a Greek island near Athens, site of a famous ancient sea battle.

clue.text: Short sailor and dog jump on the ice

indicators.note: short says the word for sailor loses its last letter

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: A small seaman and his pet leap onto a frozen pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating jump taking off from the back inside edge.

clue.text: Sanctuary for rock group in spring

definitions.meaning: a refuge or haven of calm amid hardship
the Manchester band of the Gallagher brothers
a fertile spot in the desert where water rises from the ground

explanation.surface: A rock band takes refuge somewhere in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a peaceful haven, a 1990s Britpop band, and a desert watering hole fed by a spring.

clue.text: Raise frame

definitions.meaning: to erect or put in place
to frame someone is to rig evidence against them

explanation.surface: Lift a picture surround.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means erect; as a noun it means a rigged trap, as when someone is framed.

clue.text: Kitchen strainer for lard, once melted

indicators.note: melted says the letters of the fat and the word after it run together into a new shape

explanation.surface: A sieve formerly used for draining melted cooking fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated bowl used for draining food, a type of kitchen strainer.

clue.text: Called chap over to meet editor

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the word for chap is turned upward

parts.note: a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A man is summoned over to meet the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Named means called by a particular name, a synonym of called.

clue.text: Unknown, some screwball

parts.note: Z is one of the unknowns in algebra
any can mean some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: A mystery person, somewhat eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany describes someone amusingly unconventional, like a screwball.

clue.text: Effects of cultivating at the farm

indicators.note: cultivating suggests working the soil, so these letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: What happens as a result of working the land on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath is the set of consequences following an event, its effects.

clue.text: Girl I love breaks arm in retreat

indicators.note: breaks says the pair of letters splits the reversed word apart from inside
in retreat says the word arm goes backwards

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman's affection cracks an arm as she withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns ARM to MRA, and 'breaks' sets IO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is a girl's name, a female first name of Irish and Scottish origin.

clue.text: Time to take off record

parts.note: to ape someone is to mimic or take them off

explanation.surface: Instruction to remove a recording after a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to make a recording of it on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Porcelain cap and hat

parts.note: a crown is the cap fitted over a damaged tooth
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: Headwear in two styles, apparently a type of china.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown Derby is fine porcelain made in Derby, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is a well-known English make of porcelain tableware.
